12. In the present case, the Review Petitioner has sought the review of the impugned order on the grounds of error apparent on the face of the record and oversight of relevant and material facts, which are dealt with in the subsequent paragraphs.

30. It is a settled position in terms of the judgment of Hon`ble Supreme Court in Parsion Devi v. Sumitra Devi reported in 1997 8 SCC 715 that the review proceedings are not by way of an appeal and have to be strictly confined to the scope and ambit of Order 47 Rule 1 of CPC and that the judgment may be open to review, inter alia, if there is a mistake or an error apparent on the face of the record and that an error which is not self-evident and has to be detected by a process of reasoning can hardly be said to be an error apparent requiring court to exercise its power of review. The Hon'ble Supreme Court also enunciated these principles in judgment in Kamlesh Verma v. Mayawati and Ors., as reported in AIR 2006 SC 75.

33. For the reasons mentioned above, we find no substance in the contentions and the grounds urged by the Review Petitioner as the same are directed against the reasoning and conclusions recorded in the order seeking re-appreciation of the material on record and a different conclusion, which deserve to be rejected and hence rejected.
